content_metadata.description: A video analysis focusing on training young soccer players in the strategy of pressing in the final third of the field, involving both instructional and practical drill demonstration elements.

qAndA.question: What color training vest did the "sweepers" wear?
How many touches did the "sweepers" have in the first iteration of the drill?

qAndA.answer: To increase the pressure on the defensive team and encourage them to apply the pressing principles without the safety net of the "sweepers."
qAndA.question: Why did the coach remove the "sweepers" from the drill?

qAndA.answer: A bad touch, a sideways pass, or a sloppy pass from the opponent.
qAndA.question: What are some cues that the players were encouraged to look for to trigger pressing?

qAndA.answer: Pressing in the final third is an important strategy for winning the ball back, but it must be done selectively and at the right times, using cues and triggers to make strategic decisions as a team.

To view this video and to have access to the printable session plan, visit:
https://thecoachingmanual.com/drill/5753952654065664

This defending session develops an understanding of when to press and when to drop off, encouraging tactical awareness, communication, and great execution. 

In this conditioned small-sided game players must translate the defending skills from the rest of the session to a realistic match scenario.
